1: Chapter 1: The Guest on a Rainy Night

It had been raining for three days straight in Doldari Village. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village's small apothecary on her own.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's earnings, snuffed out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when an urgent knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"
At the door stood a young man, soaked to the bone. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was soaked with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please treat this wound," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I'll pay you. Will three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?"
He took a letter wrapped in oiled paper from inside his robe. "I have to get this letter to Cheongpungsa by May eighteenth."
Haneul thought to herself. The neighbors were already jealous that the apothecary was doing well, and now a strange man had come knocking in the middle of the night.
Even so, Haneul refused the money and only said, "I'll guide you into the mountains early tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two set out. Haneul had a basket on her back, and inside it were rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they met the old man Lee Youngsoo chopping firewood. He set down his axe and lowered his voice. He said that the previous evening three strangers had been at the edge of the village looking for an injured young man.
"Haneul, take the side trail," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked him.
The side trail was narrow and slippery. Haneul went ahead, placing each step firmly as she went. Park Junho followed silently behind her.

By noon the rain had stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted, and the roof of Cheongpungsa came into view in the distance. A nun was standing in front of the temple gate. It was Sister Jeonghye, who greeted visitors for the temple.
Sister Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You saved my life." Haneul smiled and answered, "Then next time you come, fix the roof of the herb shop for me." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Around evening Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
